meta.status: Eight questions are answerable now with a source. Seven are not, and each names the artefact that would close it. Nothing here is a forecast.
meta.rule: A question moves to 'answered' only when the answer has a source link. An answer of 'we cannot know yet' is a legitimate answer and is recorded as such.

questions.question: Does each submitted link actually land on the product the owner meant to send readers to?
questions.what_we_have: All five submitted links resolved to a live Amazon listing when re-checked on 2026-11-20, and the arrival ASIN and title were transcribed for each (P-01..P-05).
questions.what_is_missing: The owner's intended ASIN for each. Every submitted path code is nine characters; every ASIN observed on arrival is ten. That is evidence the codes are short-link slugs rather than identifiers, so intent cannot be read off the link.
questions.how_to_close: In the Associates dashboard, open SiteStripe for each product and copy the tagged link for the exact ASIN intended, then record both values side by side.
questions.blocking: yes — every product claim downstream depends on it

questions.question: Why does one link never resolve?
questions.what_we_have: https://link.amazon/B0c8moW59 was requested three times and returned Amazon's /checkpoint/continue interstitial each time. No product page was reached.
questions.what_is_missing: Whether the short link is expired, mistyped, region-restricted, or simply challenging this particular client.
questions.how_to_close: Open it once from a normal browser on the owner's own network and note the final URL. If it is dead, re-issue the link from the Associates dashboard.
questions.blocking: no — the other four can proceed without it, but P-04 cannot be sold

questions.question: Are the clicks actually attributed to shopnow047c-20?
questions.what_we_have: The tracking ID was supplied in the brief. Nothing on any arrived-at page showed a tag parameter.
questions.what_is_missing: Nothing for identity. The remaining gap is the intended ASIN per product, which is Q-01.
questions.how_to_close: One test click on the owner's own device, then check the Associates click report for that day. That is the only permitted source for this number.
questions.blocking: no — identity is recorded; intent is not
questions.answer: Every one of the five products has an observed, ten-character ASIN recorded from the page the link reached: B0CDY277D3, B09B7SB46R, B08DKYBTPH, B0DHZTCNR5 and B0DZFD6R9Z. Whether each is the one the publisher intended is a separate question (Q-01), and is still open.
questions.evidence: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0CDY277D3 and the four other /dp/ pages in products.json

questions.question: Should the site show prices?
questions.what_we_have: Amazon's Program Policies allow showing price and availability only where Amazon serves the link carrying that data, or where it arrives via Creators API or PA API (SRC-02).
questions.what_is_missing: A decision, and if the answer is yes, API credentials.
questions.how_to_close: Either apply for API access and render Amazon-served prices only, or keep prices off the site. Both are compliant; a scraped price is not.
questions.answer: No price, star rating, review count or stock status appears anywhere on this site, because neither permitted data path is connected.
questions.blocking: no — the site is compliant without prices

questions.question: Is the disclosure in the right place?
questions.what_we_have: The Operating Agreement requires the exact statement on the site (SRC-01). The FTC says a footer-only disclosure is easy to miss and that proximity to the recommendation matters (SRC-03).
questions.what_is_missing: Nothing structural. What remains is a legal review of the wording around it, which this build cannot perform.
questions.how_to_close: A human review against SRC-01 and SRC-03. The placement itself is already above the fold on every page and repeated in the footer.
questions.answer: The required sentence sits in a strip above the masthead on every page, and repeats in the footer. Each product card carries its own one-line affiliate note so a reader who never scrolls still sees it.

questions.question: P-05 is a thermometer, not an air fryer. Does it belong in the same catalogue?
questions.what_we_have: The listing title and its category path both put P-05 under Thermometers, not Air Fryers. The other four are all under Air Fryers.
questions.what_is_missing: The owner's editorial intent — was the thermometer meant as an accessory to the air-fryer content, or as a separate line?
questions.how_to_close: One sentence from the owner. Until then the site treats it honestly: it is listed in its own section and never described as an air fryer.

questions.question: Which topics are worth writing about?
questions.what_we_have: Four editorial hypotheses, clearly labelled as hypotheses.
questions.what_is_missing: Any search data at all. No Search Console property, no impressions, no query list, no click data.
questions.how_to_close: Verify the property in Search Console, submit the sitemap, wait for impressions, then export the query report and pick topics from it. Until then the topic list is a guess and is labelled as one.
questions.blocking: no — but writing more guides before this is guessing

questions.question: Who is the author, and why should a reader trust them?
questions.what_we_have: Nothing. There is no named person, no credentials, no first-hand testing.
questions.what_is_missing: A real byline and a real basis for it. This is the single largest trust gap on the site and cannot be automated away.
questions.how_to_close: A named editor with a short, accurate bio. Claiming testing that did not happen would breach both the FTC guides and the Operating Agreement, so the bio must describe what the writer actually did.
questions.blocking: partly — it limits how much authority the guides can claim

questions.question: What is the actual commission rate for these categories?
questions.what_we_have: Nothing. The rate card sits behind an Associates sign-in.
questions.how_to_close: Read it in the Associates dashboard and record it. It is deliberately blank here rather than copied from a blog.
questions.blocking: no — but no revenue estimate is possible without it, so none is given

questions.question: Is the analytics endpoint live, and is it lawful to switch on?
questions.what_we_have: The five event names and a client that stays silent by default.
questions.what_is_missing: An endpoint, a privacy notice, a retention period, and a decision on consent for visitors in jurisdictions that require it.
questions.how_to_close: Publish the privacy notice first, then deploy the collector, then enable the beacon. The order matters.
questions.blocking: yes, for measurement — the site works without it

questions.question: Can this site be indexed at all, given the repository path?
questions.what_we_have: The site is served from a project path on github.io. All internal links resolve within that path and the sitemap lists the same host.
questions.what_is_missing: Verification that the sitemap has been submitted and that pages are actually being crawled.
questions.how_to_close: Search Console verification, then sitemap submission, then check coverage after a few days.
questions.blocking: no — but nothing will rank until it happens

questions.question: Does the site make any claim it cannot support?
questions.what_we_have: Every page was machine-checked for banned patterns: no price figure, no star rating, no review count, no stock status, no superlative, no test claim.
questions.what_is_missing: A human read for tone and implication — a checker cannot catch a sentence that is technically true but suggests more.
questions.how_to_close: Read the three guides and the product pages once with the question 'what would a sceptical reader infer?'
questions.answer: No page claims testing, ranking or a winner. Every product page says plainly that the product was not tested.

questions.question: What happens if the owner never supplies the missing account data?
questions.what_we_have: A site that is compliant but thin: five product records, four of them identified, honest guides, no prices.
questions.what_is_missing: A decision about how long to wait.
questions.how_to_close: This is an owner decision, not a research one. The site is built to be safe to leave running in this state indefinitely.
questions.answer: Nothing on the site breaks. It stays accurate because it claims so little. The cost of the missing data is opportunity, not correctness.
questions.evidence: No external source: this is a conclusion about the build's own contents, not a citation. Stated plainly so it is not mistaken for one.

questions.question: Are the supplied links Special Links in the sense the agreement means?
questions.what_we_have: Four resolve to live Amazon listings. None showed a tag on arrival.
questions.what_is_missing: Confirmation that each is tagged with shopnow047c-20. The agreement requires Special Links to use the assigned Associates ID (SRC-02).
questions.how_to_close: Re-issue each destination as a tagged link from SiteStripe and replace the outbound URL after recording both the old and new value.
questions.blocking: yes — this is the difference between a link and a commission

questions.question: Is there any traffic, and where would it come from?
questions.what_we_have: Nothing. No analytics, no Search Console, no referral data.
questions.how_to_close: Turn on measurement (Q-10) and verification (Q-11) before assuming any channel works.
questions.blocking: no — but every revenue assumption depends on it

questions.question: Which topics should the site write about next, and what is the evidence for them?
questions.what_we_have: Six guides exist, all written from editorial judgement. None was chosen from a search query report, because no query report exists yet.
questions.what_is_missing: A Search Console performance report or a Bing Webmaster report for the site, covering impressions, clicks and the queries that produced them.
questions.how_to_close: Verify the property in Search Console and submit the sitemap (S-07). Submit the same sitemap to Bing Webmaster Tools (S-13). Re-read the query report after four weeks and pick the next topic from the queries that already produce impressions but few clicks.
questions.blocking: no — the site can publish, but each new topic is a guess until this exists
